group.passage: Vincent van Gogh’s “The Starry Night” is one of the best-known paintings in the world. In the two texts below, an art historian explains how the picture came to be, and a physicist describes what scientists have discovered in its swirling sky more than a century later.

passage_parts.label: A
passage_parts.title: Painting a Feeling
passage_parts.text: Van Gogh completed “The Starry Night” in June 1889, during the year he spent at a hospital in Saint-Rémy, a small town in the south of France. From his bedroom window he watched the hills and fields by day and by night, and that view became the starting point of the picture. Yet the finished work is far from a simple record of it, for he combined the view with scenes that existed only in his mind. A quiet village sleeps beneath the hills, and a dark cypress tree rises in the foreground like a flame. Above them, the whole sky seems to roll and boil. Stars glow inside bright rings of light, and most of the canvas is painted in deep blues, lit here and there by touches of yellow and white. Van Gogh never aimed for a precise copy of the scene; what he wanted to capture was the feeling that the night stirred in him. Today the painting hangs in the Museum of Modern Art in New York.

passage_parts.label: B
passage_parts.title: Hidden Order in the Swirls
passage_parts.text: As a physicist, I study turbulent flow, the irregular motion of air and water that you can see in rising smoke or a fast river. Few paintings capture restless motion as vividly as this one. In the 1940s, the Russian mathematician Andrei Kolmogorov showed that such flow hides a kind of order, with large eddies breaking into smaller ones in a predictable way. In 2006, researchers in Mexico found the same pattern in the way brightness changes across the painting. A study published in 2024 went further, showing that the sizes of its fourteen main swirls also fit Kolmogorov’s description. Yet van Gogh died more than a decade before Kolmogorov was even born. No one suggests that the painter knew the mathematics, and a still picture can never literally contain moving air. Perhaps he simply studied clouds and the sky with great care. In that sense, he was ahead of his time, recording with paint a pattern that science would describe only decades later.

translation_zh.text:
文森．梵谷的〈星夜〉是世界上最有名的畫作之一。在下面兩篇短文中，一位藝術史學者說明這幅畫是怎麼誕生的，一位物理學者則描述科學家在一個多世紀後，從畫中旋轉的天空裡發現了什麼。

Text A　畫出一種感受
梵谷在 1889 年 6 月完成〈星夜〉，當時他正在法國南部小鎮聖雷米的一家醫院度過一年。他從臥室窗戶日夜看著窗外的山丘和田野，那片景色成了這幅畫的起點。然而，完成的作品遠不只是那片景色的單純紀錄，因為他把那片景色和只存在於自己腦海中的景象結合在一起。一座寧靜的村莊在山丘下沉睡，一棵深色的柏樹像火焰般在前景竄起。在它們上方，整片天空彷彿在翻騰、沸騰。星星在明亮的光圈裡發光，畫布大部分是深藍色，各處點綴著黃色和白色。梵谷從來不追求精確地複製眼前的景色；他想捕捉的，是夜晚在他心中激起的感受。如今這幅畫掛在紐約的現代藝術博物館。

Text B　漩渦中隱藏的秩序
身為物理學者，我研究的是亂流，也就是你在上升的煙或湍急的河流中看得到的、空氣和水不規則的運動。很少有畫作能像這幅畫一樣，把躁動的流動捕捉得如此生動。1940 年代，俄國數學家柯莫哥洛夫證明這種流動隱藏著某種秩序：大的渦旋會以可預測的方式分裂成較小的渦旋。2006 年，墨西哥的研究人員在畫中亮度變化的方式裡發現了同樣的模式。2024 年發表的一項研究更進一步，發現畫中十四個主要漩渦的大小也符合柯莫哥洛夫的描述。然而，梵谷去世十多年後，柯莫哥洛夫才出生。沒有人認為這位畫家懂得那些數學，而且靜止的畫作永遠不可能真的包含流動的空氣。或許他只是非常用心地研究雲和天空。就這個意義來說，他走在時代的前面，用顏料記錄下科學要到幾十年後才描述出來的模式。
